# The Model {#sec-model}

The model is kept deliberately small: two definitions per axis, each
with its credited home stated inline, and nothing else. Every object
below is mechanized in Lean 4; identifiers are given so a reader can
locate the corresponding declaration, but nothing in this section
depends on Lean syntax to be read.

## Records, contexts, and claims

A **record** is a finite, append-only sequence of entries,
$\Record := \mathrm{List}\ \mathit{Entry}$, ordered by the prefix
relation $\sqsubseteq$: $w \sqsubseteq w'$ iff $w$ is a prefix of $w'$.
Records grow only by appending — nothing already committed is ever
edited or removed. A **context** $\Context$ is an abstract, inhabited,
non-trivial type standing for everything a verifier does *not* see:
causal history, wall-clock time, key custody, the existence of other
records. A **world** pairs the two, $\World := \Record \times \Context$.

A **claim** is a predicate over a world,
$\Claim : \Record \to \Context \to \mathrm{Prop}$ — "the entry at
position $k$ was authored by principal $A$," "record $w$ is the
canonical log's current head." The claim, not the record alone, is what
a verifier is asked to check.

## The offline verifier

A **commitment** $\Gamma$ packages a record's committed representation:
a component type $C$ (e.g. a digest), a binding relation, and a
verification-certificate type $VC$ with soundness and completeness
conditions relative to $C$. A **scheme** for $\Claim$ under $\Gamma$ is a
certificate type together with a verifier
$V : \mathit{Comm} \to \mathit{Proof} \to \mathrm{Prop}$ that decides,
from the commitment and a certificate alone — never from the record or
the context directly — whether $\Claim$ holds. This is the paper's one
modeling commitment: **the verifier's type is the offline property**.
Asking whether $\Claim$ admits a scheme is exactly asking whether
$\Claim$ can be checked from a committed digest and a certificate, with
no further access to history.

Two verifiers of the same commitment can disagree about how much they
trust what they see; the model distinguishes exactly two soundness
flavors, both defined over the same scheme machinery:

- **Snapshot-sound**: the certificate is valid for the record as it
  stood at the moment the certificate was produced. Nothing is claimed
  about what happens as the record grows.
- **Enduring-sound**: the certificate remains valid for every extension
  of the record. A certificate produced today keeps verifying against
  tomorrow's, larger record.

The distinction is not cosmetic. @sec-theorem's factorization display
turns on exactly this split: it is what lets a single classical notion —
"observable property," bundling semi-decidability with stability — pull
apart into two independent axes in this setting (@sec-factorization).

## Verifier strata

A scheme's certificate and verifier are graded by the computational
power required to run them. This paper uses three strata, in
decreasing generality:

- $\oracle$ — no computability constraint; the verifier may decide
  anything.
- $\computable$ — the verifier's components are computable, over a
  `Primcodable` alphabet.
- $\polynomial$ — the verifier runs in polynomial time and the
  certificate has polynomial size.

A fourth, intermediate stratum — requiring only classical decidability
of the commitment's equality test — turns out to add no content:
classical decidability is universal by
$\texttt{Classical.propDecidable}$, so its verdicts coincide exactly
with the oracle stratum's. It survives in the mechanization as
constructive scaffolding that de-risked the computable stratum, credited
honestly rather than presented as a fourth distinct grade. The tower
used throughout is $\oracle \supset \computable \supset \polynomial$;
the polynomial stratum's theorems remain open (@sec-theorem).

## The three axes

Three independent conditions on a claim $\Claim$, each defined once,
without reference to any scheme:

**Determination.**
$\Det(\Claim) := \forall\, w\; \xi\; \xi',\ \Claim\ w\ \xi \leftrightarrow \Claim\ w\ \xi'$
— the claim's truth value does not depend on the context, only on the
record. Equivalently, $\Claim$ factors through the projection that
forgets context: $\Det(\Claim) \leftrightarrow \exists\, \psi,\ \Claim =
(\lambda\, w\; \_.\ \psi\ w)$, membership in the image of the pullback
$\pstar$ along that projection. Where $\Det(\Claim)$ holds, write
$\phihat$ for the resulting record-only predicate.

**Certifiability** (at stratum $Q$). Whether $\phihat$ is
semi-decidable/certifiable at $Q$'s computational power — $\Sigma_1$ at
the computable stratum, $\mathrm{NP}$ with genuine size and time bounds
at the polynomial one. (This axis was previously named "decidability";
@sec-related-work explains the rename.)

**Monotonicity.**
$\Mono(\Claim) := \forall\, w\; w'\; \xi,\ \Claim\ w\ \xi \to w \sqsubseteq w' \to \Claim\ w'\ \xi$
— once true, a claim stays true as the record is extended. For
determined $\Claim$ this is equivalent to $\phihat$ being upward-closed
under $\sqsubseteq$: $\UpC(\psi) := \forall\, w\; w',\ w \sqsubseteq w'
\to \psi\ w \to \psi\ w'$.

These three conditions are the paper's entire vocabulary. Everything
that follows is a statement about how they combine.
